recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core FHIR source follow-up is needed for FHIR-26687 unless the work group later revises the broader multiline-prescription and Request pattern guidance together.
issue_request: FHIR-26687 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5 by Pharmacy. It asked how repeated v2 RXR segments for one ORC/RXO should map to MedicationRequest.dosageInstruction, how either/or options are represented, and how two alternative MedicationRequests are linked. The accepted guidance was to create multiple MedicationRequest instances, use MedicationRequest.groupIdentifier to group them, set each MedicationRequest.intent to option, add examples, and clarify the MedicationRequest.dosageInstruction wording.
initial_application: Commit b9257918056a31ebdc080627432cc94db78637e0, merged by 7683bfb3d7eb6917f2c3cd6c0a1414fa0518f977, explicitly listed FHIR-26687 and added the paired medrx0343a and medrx0343b MedicationRequest examples plus example-list entries for same-drug route options using the same groupIdentifier and intent=option. The detailed grouping prose around dosageInstruction was already present from the closely related FHIR-27885 guidance.
additional_context: MedicationRequest is active in source/fhir.ini. Current medicationrequest-introduction.xml and medicationrequest-notes.xml retain guidance that MedicationRequest requests one medication, multiple requested items use multiple instances, groupIdentifier groups independently manageable requests, and RequestOrchestration is used for complex optional or timing relationships. Later R6 dosage work changed MedicationRequest.dosageInstruction to DosageDetails and moved the long grouping explanation from the ElementDefinition comment into narrative guidance. FHIR-27885 has already been audited on the combined branch; FHIR-47251 is a broader Resolved-change-required multiline-prescription issue and was not decided here.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current active source already preserves the seed result through paired examples and nearby grouping guidance, while current RequestOrchestration wording reflects related accepted grouping guidance rather than a missed FHIR-26687 application.
